answer: The dredger measures the silt in every reach before the bucket bites, and the survey files the depth beside the date for the whole canal. A sable reach claimed as dredged fails the survey: the bucket must have bitten at the vertex of the reach, and a reach never dredged has no depth to show. Faking a season of dredging means hiring a crew, faking eighty soundings and paying 17,800, and the gale survey is checked against the barges' own draughts, so a reach whose silt was never measured grounds the first boat through.
